label: Bansal S01: opioid with alcohol dependence
title: Ongoing opioid with a history of alcohol dependence
statement: Persistent prescription of opioid analgesics to a patient with a medical history of alcohol addiction, abuse, or dependence [32, 47–49]

source.document: Bansal N, et al. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care. BMC Med 2024;22:5, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x
source.credit: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x

plain_summary: Taking an opioid pain medicine over a long time is riskier for a person with a history of alcohol misuse or dependence.

medicine_groups.name: Opioid pain medicines
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, patches and injections used for pain count. Codeine combined with paracetamol counts, for example Panadeine Forte. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Count methadone when the product and record support use for pain. Ask for the indication if it is unclear. Exclude methadone and buprenorphine used for opioid dependence. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count only opioid analgesics used for pain in the source population. If the indication is unknown, report at most a possible finding and ask what the product was used for. Exclude substitution treatment and codeine cough preparations. Count Physeptone tablets or Opod-D Syrup when use for pain is supported. Confirm the use of Opod-D Syrup before counting it. Exclude Opod-P Liquid, Physeptone Liquid and Biodone Forte. Use documented course dates first. Otherwise use quantities, directions and supply dates to assess duration. If gaps or unclear directions leave continuity uncertain, ask how much was used, how often and for how long.

needs_facts.what: History of alcohol addiction, abuse or dependence
needs_facts.meets: Any of these conditions was present before or during the opioid course, including a past condition in remission.

options.words: Present before or during this opioid course
No such history before or during this course

needs_facts.what: Reason for the opioid course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if the product and record leave its purpose unclear and the other evidence fits. Only chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care qualifies for this course. An unknown reason leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding in a person over 18 at supply when the record shows alcohol addiction, abuse or dependence before or during the course and more than one Group A opioid prescription for pain in one treatment course lasting at least three months. Give no finding at age 18 or younger, with a recorded absence of that history, for opioids prescribed for cancer pain or palliative care, for substitution treatment or codeine cough preparations, or for separate short courses. If the other evidence fits, report only a possible finding and check any missing age, alcohol history or reason for this opioid course, or check continuity when repeated supplies span at least three months but the course remains unclear.
cannot_be_seen: Current alcohol use, why the opioid was started, doses taken, and care given by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the opioid is still needed and safe for this person, and support for alcohol use if relevant.
